questions.question: A sum of money amounts to Rs 9800 after 5 years and to Rs 12005 after 8 years at the same rate of simple interest. Find the principal.
questions.solution:
SI for (8 − 5) = 3 years = 12005 − 9800 = Rs 2205, so SI per year = 2205 / 3 = Rs 735.
SI for 5 years = 5 × 735 = 3675. Principal = 9800 − 3675 = **Rs 6125**.
questions.trick: **SI for T years = (1-year interest) × T.** Difference of two amounts gives interest for the gap in years directly; peel off SI to reach the principal.

questions.question: The difference between the compound interest and the simple interest on a certain sum for 2 years at 10% per annum is Rs 60. Find the sum.
questions.trick: **CI − SI (2 yrs) = P(R/100)^2.** The extra is just interest-on-interest of one year.

questions.question: Find the compound interest on Rs 25000 at 12% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually.
questions.trick: **CI for 2 years = (2R + R^2/100)% of P** — no need to compute amounts separately.

questions.question: A shopkeeper marks his goods 40% above the cost price and then allows a discount of 10%. Find his profit percent.
questions.trick: **SP = CP × multiplier chain.** Chain markup and discount as multipliers; the base is always CP.

questions.question: By selling an article for Rs 720, a man loses 10%. At what price should he sell it to gain 15%?
questions.trick: **Base is CP; SP = CP × multiplier.** Recover CP from the loss SP first, then re-apply the gain multiplier.

questions.question: A trader sells two articles for Rs 990 each. On one he gains 10% and on the other he loses 10%. Find his overall loss or profit percent.
questions.trick: Equal SP with equal +x% and −x% always gives a **net loss of (x^2/100)%**. Here 10^2/100 = 1%.

questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 12 days and B can do the same work in 18 days. Working together, in how many days will they finish it?
questions.solution: LCM(12, 18) = 36 units. Rates: A = 3, B = 2, together = 5 units/day. Time = 36/5 = **7.2 days**.
questions.trick: **LCM method** — set total work = LCM of the days, convert each worker to units/day, add rates.

questions.question: A and B together can complete a work in 15 days. A alone can do it in 20 days. In how many days can B alone complete the work?
questions.solution: Total work = LCM(15, 20) = 60. Together = 4, A = 3, so B = 4 − 3 = 1 unit/day. Time = 60/1 = **60 days**.
questions.trick: **B's rate = (combined rate) − (A's rate)** on the LCM units.

questions.question: 12 men can complete a piece of work in 8 days. How many men are required to complete the same work in 6 days?
questions.solution: Total work = 12 × 8 = 96 man-days. Men needed for 6 days = 96/6 = **16**.
questions.trick: **Men × Days = constant** (M1·D1 = M2·D2) when the work is fixed.

questions.question: A train 180 m long is running at 72 km/hr. How long will it take to cross a platform 220 m long?
questions.solution: Speed = 72 × 5/18 = 20 m/s. Distance to cross = 180 + 220 = 400 m. Time = 400/20 = **20 s**.
questions.trick: **km/hr → m/s: multiply by 5/18.** To cross a platform, distance = train length + platform length.

questions.question: A boat goes 24 km downstream in 3 hours and returns the same distance upstream in 4 hours. Find the speed of the boat in still water.
questions.solution: Downstream = 24/3 = 8 km/hr, upstream = 24/4 = 6 km/hr. Still-water speed = (8 + 6)/2 = **7 km/hr**.
questions.trick: **Boat speed = (down + up)/2**, stream speed = (down − up)/2.

questions.question: A person travels from A to B at 40 km/hr and returns at 60 km/hr along the same route. Find the average speed for the whole journey.
questions.trick: **Equal distance both ways → average speed = 2xy/(x+y)** (harmonic mean), never the plain average.

questions.question: The average of 5 numbers is 27. If one of the numbers is excluded, the average of the remaining becomes 25. Find the excluded number.
questions.trick: **Sum = average × count.** Work with totals, then subtract.

questions.question: The average age of 11 players of a cricket team is 28 years. If the coach's age is included, the average increases by 2 years. Find the coach's age.
questions.solution: New average = 30 for 12 people → total = 360. Old total = 11 × 28 = 308. Coach = 360 − 308 = **52**.
questions.trick: new member's value = **new average + (increase × old count)** = 30 + 2 × 11 = 52.

questions.question: Find the average of the first 20 multiples of 7.
questions.solution: Average of first n multiples of k = k(n+1)/2 = 7 × 21/2 = **73.5**.
questions.trick: **Average of first n multiples of k = k(n+1)/2**; for an evenly spaced list, average = (first + last)/2 = (7 + 140)/2.

questions.question: The ratio of the present ages of A and B is 5 : 7. After 6 years the ratio becomes 3 : 4. Find A's present age.
questions.trick: Convert the ratio to 5x, 7x, add the years, cross-multiply the new ratio, solve for x.

questions.question: The present age of a father is three times that of his son. After 5 years, the father's age will be two and a half times the son's age. Find the son's present age.
questions.trick: Express both current ages in one variable, add the same years to each, then equate to the new multiple.

questions.question: Divide Rs 1200 among A, B and C in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5. Find C's share.
questions.trick: **Each share = (its ratio part / total parts) × total amount.**

questions.question: If a : b = 3 : 4 and b : c = 6 : 5, find a : b : c.
questions.trick: **Scale each ratio so the linking term (b) matches** (LCM of 4 and 6 = 12), then read straight across.

questions.question: In an election between two candidates, the winner secured 60% of the valid votes and won by 900 votes. Assuming all votes were valid, find the total number of votes polled.
questions.solution: Winner 60%, loser 40%; margin = 20% of total = 900 → total = 900 × 100/20 = **4500**.
questions.trick: **Winning margin % = (win% − lose%)**; total = margin votes × 100 / margin%.

questions.question: The price of an item is increased by 25%. By what percent should the new price be reduced to bring it back to the original price?
questions.trick: To undo an x% rise, reduce by **x/(100 + x) × 100%**. (For 25% it is the classic 20%.)

questions.question: In what ratio must rice costing Rs 30 per kg be mixed with rice costing Rs 45 per kg so that the mixture is worth Rs 35 per kg?
questions.trick: **Alligation cross** — cheaper : dearer = (dearer − mean) : (mean − cheaper).

questions.question: A vessel contains 40 litres of pure milk. 4 litres is drawn out and replaced with water; this process is repeated once more. Find the quantity of milk left in the vessel.
questions.trick: **Replacement (repeated) formula: final = initial × (1 − removed/total)^n.**

questions.question: A starts a business with Rs 20000. After 6 months, B joins with Rs 30000. At the end of the year, find the ratio in which the profit should be divided between A and B.
questions.trick: **Profit share ∝ capital × months invested.** Weight each partner by money-time, then reduce.

questions.question: A, B and C invest Rs 6000, Rs 8000 and Rs 10000 respectively in a business for one year. If the total annual profit is Rs 7200, find C's share.
questions.trick: Same duration → **profit ratio = investment ratio**; each share = (part/total) × profit.
